text_blocks.snippet: To know if you have COVID-19, monitor for symptoms and consider testing, especially if you've been exposed or have symptoms. Common symptoms include fever, cough, shortness of breath, sore throat, congestion, fatigue, and loss of taste or smell according to the CDC. Over-the-counter (OTC) COVID-19 tests can be used at home, and it's recommended to repeat testing after a negative result, even without symptoms, to reduce the risk of false negatives.

text_blocks.snippet: To test for COVID-19, you can use either a viral test (like NAAT or PCR) or an antigen test. Viral tests, including NAATs (which are considered the "gold standard"), are highly accurate and can detect even low levels of the virus, but results may take up to 3 days as samples are typically sent to a lab. Antigen tests are faster, with results often available in minutes, but may be less sensitive, especially with low viral loads or if performed too early in the infection. If you suspect you have COVID-19, consult with a healthcare professional or local health authority for guidance on the most appropriate testing method and when and where to get tested.
